headline_marked: [[Bangladesh can qualify for World Cup]], says Argentine legend Caniggia, praising nation's 'best' passion
headline: Bangladesh can qualify for World Cup, says Argentine legend Caniggia, praising nation's 'best' passion
summary: Argentine football legend Claudio Caniggia, during his visit to Dhaka, expressed his admiration for Bangladesh's footballing hopes and the extraordinary passion for Argentina, calling the fans 'one of the best'.
details: Argentine football legend Claudio Caniggia met budding Bangladeshi footballers at the Fortis Football Academy in Dhaka on Monday. He was visiting as the guest of honour at the Pillow Chips Dhaka Interschool Champions League (DICL) 2026, where he handed out prizes.

Caniggia received a very warm welcome and expressed his enjoyment of Bangladesh's passionate people. He noted he wasn't surprised by the strong following for Argentina, especially after the 1986 World Cup and Diego Maradona's era.

Regarding Bangladesh's World Cup qualification hopes, Caniggia acknowledged it's a 'long way' but expressed optimism. He believes with the tournament expanding, and proper development, Bangladesh could have the opportunity to qualify.

Caniggia described Bangladeshi fans as 'one of the best' due to their intense passion. He observed they 'suffer when Argentina suffer' and celebrate victories with unmatched enthusiasm, unlike supporters in other countries.

He also shared personal anecdotes, including his friendship with Diego Maradona and their famous kiss, calling it 'something natural'. Caniggia also recounted his controversial red card at the 2002 World Cup, attributing it to a referee's mistake.
The legend reflected on the privilege of Argentina having two of football's greatest players, Maradona and Messi, alongside Pelé. He emphasized this as a significant source of pride for his nation.

Caniggia also addressed Argentina's loss in the 2026 World Cup final to Spain, stating his disappointment but acknowledging Spain deserved the win. He noted Argentina's team was fatigued and had injured players, while Spain played better.

headline_marked: [[Rabiul succeeds in sheep farming]], earns BDT 40 lakh annually in Nilphamari
headline: Rabiul succeeds in sheep farming, earns BDT 40 lakh annually in Nilphamari
summary: Rabiul Islam's 'Niyoti Dumba Farm' in Syedpur, Nilphamari, has grown from a small initiative to a thriving business. His success story is inspiring many in the community to take up sheep rearing.
details: Rabiul Islam (54) from Katharipara village in Syedpur, Nilphamari, has achieved self-sufficiency through his 'Niyoti Dumba Farm'. Starting with just a few sheep, his venture now boasts 60 animals and generates an annual income of approximately BDT 40 lakh.

Rabiul's elder brother, Rezaul Islam, who moved to Saudi Arabia after their farming efforts failed, inspired the idea. Rezaul brought two sheep during a visit in 2022 and later added six more, marking the beginning of Rabiul's farm with 'Turkey' and 'Awasi' breeds.

These sheep breeds are known for their good reproductive capacity, giving birth twice a year. This rapid breeding allowed the farm's population to quickly grow, reaching 65 within two years before sales commenced. The sheep have also adapted well to Bangladesh's climate.

The farm features a two-room shed with a wooden slatted floor, designed to keep the area clean by allowing waste to fall through. Sixty sheep, both large and small, roam freely in the open space, tended by two daily wage shepherds.

Sheep primarily feed on tender grass, supplemented with oilcake, bran, straw, and molasses-soaked silage. Rabiul sells around 30 sheep annually, both online and directly, with prices ranging from BDT 80,000 to BDT 2.5 lakh, depending on their 50-80 kg weight.

He also sells sheep meat, priced at BDT 3,000 per kg, to meet local demand. Wholesalers from Dhaka and other divisional cities purchase sheep from his farm, with some even acquiring them for their own rearing initiatives.

Syedpur Upazila Livestock Officer Md. Abu Kaes Bin Aziz notes the farm's potential to meet meat demand, stating that the livestock department is monitoring it and observes minimal disease issues. Rabiul's success has inspired many neighbors to consider sheep farming, recognizing its low maintenance costs and high profitability.
